spec.title: Standard: minimal intervention in the fork

status.comment: edition 0.2.0; norms are UPPER-KEBAB anchors, rationale is lower-kebab; distilled from a first rebranding pilot in 2026 and the parallel-system rulings of 2026-09-07

p.MI-SCOPE: The standard applies to every patch set maintained by codkit: to a delta artifact of any layer and to any own code delivered into the fork tree.

p.MI-THE-MEASURE: The measure of an intervention is not the directory a file lives in but the number of upstream points that must stay unchanged for the intervention to keep working: an export name, the shape of a record, an id, a load order, the body of a method — each such point counts.

source-norm.title: 1. Where the layer norm comes from

p.MI-LAYER-LADDER-IS-CODKIT: The layer ladder and the choice rule come from codkit, not from this standard: the highest applicable layer of `own → service-override → entry-module → config-overlay → resource-file → rewrite-rule → patch` (PROP-005 §1, anchor `LAYER-CHOICE-RULE`, file `<codkit-tool-root>/vibevm/vibespecs/modules/codkit/PROP-005-delta-layers.xml`) and the decision tree in `<codkit-tool-root>/docs/codkit/protocol/human/03-interventions.md`. The standard restates neither and opens no second ladder.

p.MI-DESCENT-NEEDS-A-NAMED-REASON: Descending a layer is allowed only with a named reason: why not own, why not a service override, why not an overlay — in the terms of the decision tree, never "it was simpler".

p.MI-NECESSITY-WINS: Necessity wins over minimality: a feature the product requires is implemented even where only an invasive layer can express it — for example, localising a surface that upstream never localises. Minimality then means the least invasive form of that necessary intervention, never its omission; and an existing intervention that can be made less invasive is made less invasive.

p.why-necessity-wins: A standard that could veto a required feature would be routed around, and the routing would be the silent choice this standard exists to prevent; naming the least invasive form keeps the choice visible without denying the feature.

presented-choice.title: 2. The choice is presented, never made silently

p.MI-REASON-NAMES-THE-REJECTED-LEAF: The `reason` field of an artifact of any layer below own begins with the rejected upper leaf and why it was rejected, in the form `not <leaf>: <reason>; …` — for example `not own: bootstrap before DI, no graft; not overlay: the target is not JSON` — and only then describes the intervention itself.

p.MI-LOCAL-WORK-IS-RECORDED-BEFORE-COMMIT: An intervention that appeared during the work with no home in the product's specs (no FEAT requires it) gets either a FEAT entry or a four-field decision record in the product's specs before it is committed; an intervention known only to the inventory counts as unrecorded.

p.why-silent-choices-compound: A first rebranding pilot brought three interventions its feature spec never knew of — a locale operation in the overlay and two patches under it; each was reasonable, and none could be reviewed, because the reason stayed in its author's head.

own-coupling.title: 3. The three degrees of own-code coupling

p.MI-OWN-THREE-DEGREES: Own code distinguishes three degrees of coupling to upstream: (a) the public extension API; (b) core registries and DI named in the product's seam map (§6); (c) the internals of upstream modules — mutating exported structures, depending on load order, on a field name, on a record id.

p.MI-INTERNALS-ARE-PATCH-EQUIVALENT: Own code of degree (c) counts as a patch equivalent: a mandatory contract test (`contractTests` of the record is non-empty and the test checks the observable result), a row in the seam map, a `reason` per §2; in the metric of §7 it is counted together with `rewrite-rule` and `patch`, wherever the file lives.

p.why-own-is-not-free: Moving the mutation of an upstream walkthrough array from a patch into an own module removed not one coupling point — the export name, the record shape, the record id and the load order stayed the same four; all that changed was where the failure surfaces: from the 3-way merge at `sync` to the moment the product starts.

p.MI-OWN-NEVER-THROWS-AT-MODULE-EVALUATION: Own code never throws while a module is evaluated and never brings a process down over a missing upstream point: when the expected record or export is absent it degrades to upstream behaviour; the loud failure is the guards' job (contract tests, the static proof), not the product runtime's.

p.why-degrade-not-throw: A block that throws when a walkthrough entry is missing keeps the whole workbench from starting on a future pin where that entry was renamed — over the title of one walkthrough.

channel-per-process.title: 4. One channel per process; bootstrap has none

p.MI-ONE-GRAFT-PER-PROCESS: A graft of own code (the entry-module layer, PROP-005 §3 `OWN-GRAFT-POINT`) reaches only the process whose entry it edits: renderer, main, shared process, server, CLI — each with its own entry and, if own code is needed there, its own graft.

p.MI-BOOTSTRAP-HAS-NO-CHANNEL: Bootstrap code that runs before DI (in VS Code, `src/main.ts` and what it calls before the services exist) has no channel: an intervention there is always a patch, and its `reason` calls it a patch instead of dressing it as own code.

p.MI-GRAFT-SET-IS-NAMED-WHOLE: The constant graft set — the entry graft, the lint target for the own directory, the confirmation of the tsconfig/layering/test/nls globs, the decision on header hygiene — is named as a whole at the first own module, not one item at a time as things break; its size does not grow with the amount of own code (PROP-005 §11 `CONSTANT-GRAFT-SET`).

p.why-the-set-is-named-whole: "One import line" in fact cost a graft, a lint target, a ruling on a red header check over own tests and a check of the globs; the price named as a whole compares honestly with two title patches, the price named one item at a time does not.

two-channels.title: 5. An interface string has two channels

p.MI-STRING-HAS-TWO-CHANNELS: Every interface string lives in two channels: the English text in the source (`localize(key, "…")`, an index into `nls.messages.json` in the build) and the translation in the language pack (data under the same key). An intervention that closes one channel names the fate of the other.

p.MI-NLS-KEY-CHANGE-NEEDS-A-PACK-DECISION: Changing or adding an nls key in a patch is allowed only together with a recorded language-pack decision: the product's own pack carries the translation of the new key, or the key is kept and the pack translates the upstream string, or it is recorded that a translation is deliberately absent; the decision is a decision record in the product's specs. Where upstream localises nothing at all, the invasive route is the necessary one (§1 `MI-NECESSITY-WINS`) and the record says so.

p.why-two-channels: Patches that renamed keys with a private suffix made the branded strings untranslatable for good: any future language pack shows the English branded string; had the keys been kept, the pack would have shown a translation carrying the upstream name. Both outcomes are bad, and neither had been named.

p.MI-SEAM-MAP-REQUIRED: The product keeps a seam map in its specs: for every upstream seam the delta leans on — the codkit layer, what breaks when the pin moves, what catches it; the map is dated to the pin and cited from the product's boot.

p.MI-SEAM-MAP-IS-RANKED: Seams are ordered by how far upstream sanctions them: a pull request upstream (layer 0, outside the delta) → product configuration (`product.json`) → the public extension API and built-in extensions → resources → core registries and DI through a graft → the entry of a process → build and hygiene targets → bootstrap, a method body, a literal (patch) → the internals of upstream modules (patch equivalent); a new intervention looks for the most sanctioned seam that expresses it.

p.MI-SEAM-MAP-REVALIDATED-PER-PIN: On every upgrade cycle the map is re-validated on the new pin: until confirmed it is marked "needs re-validation"; a row whose seam vanished or moved leads to a review of the intervention, not to a silent carry-over.

p.seam-map-template-lead: The map is a table; the columns are mandatory, the rows are each product's own:

tr.td: Breaks when the pin moves if…

td.ROW-EXAMPLE-INTERNALS: internals of an upstream module used from own code

tr.td: anything; the failure is at runtime

p.MI-METRIC-FALLS: The intervention metric is the number of `rewrite-rule` and `patch` artifacts plus the own records marked as patch equivalents, per subsystem; it must fall from cycle to cycle (PROP-005 §1 `LAYER-METRIC`), and the de-intrusion iteration of `03-interventions.md` runs on every upgrade cycle.

p.conformance-lead: The intervention reviewer checks conformance by observable facts, not by assurances:

facts.CONF-REASONS-NAME-REJECTED-LEAVES: In `codkit inventory --md` the `reason` of every artifact below own begins with the rejected upper leaf (§2).
facts.CONF-EVERY-INTERVENTION-HAS-A-SPEC-HOME: Every inventory id is mentioned in a product FEAT or in a decision record (§2).
facts.CONF-NECESSARY-INVASIVE-WORK-IS-NAMED: Every invasive intervention that a required feature forced names that necessity in its `reason`, and the less invasive form was looked for (§1).
facts.CONF-NO-OWN-MODULE-THROWS-AT-IMPORT: No own module throws at import: the guards cover a missing upstream point by degradation, not by an exception (§3).
facts.CONF-PATCH-EQUIVALENT-OWN-HAS-A-GUARD: Own code of degree (c) carries a non-empty `contractTests` and a seam-map row (§3).
facts.CONF-NLS-CHANGES-HAVE-A-PACK-DECISION: Every patch that changes an nls key cites a language-pack decision record (§5).
facts.CONF-SEAM-MAP-IS-DATED-TO-THE-PIN: The seam map exists, is dated to the current pin and is not marked "needs re-validation" (§6).
facts.CONF-PATCHES-ARE-GRAFTS: Every patch of type `hook` carries at most three lines of code between its markers and at least one line that imports or calls own code (§9); `codkit verify` reports `CK-E-HOOK-TOO-LARGE` otherwise.
facts.CONF-OWN-PASSES-UPSTREAM-LINT: Own code passes upstream's own lint and layering rules with the single authorship-header exemption; the exemption is one intervention with contract evidence (§9, §11).
facts.CONF-FEATURE-HAS-A-FLAG-OR-A-REASON: Every feature folder declares a flag, or its decision record names why this feature has none (§10).
facts.CONF-COLD-FEATURES-DECLARED: Every feature that cannot toggle live is declared cold (`hotToggle: false`), so a change of its flag asks for a restart instead of half-applying (§10).

parallel-system.title: 9. The delta is a parallel system

p.parallel-system-lead: Upstream itself builds a second product on the same core as a top-level layer above the workbench, with its own entries, services, contributions and an enforced import graph. A product's delta follows that precedent: it is a parallel system in upstream's own style, connected to the fork by the fewest possible grafts — never a pile of patches with logic inside them.

facts.MI-PARALLEL-SYSTEM-FIRST: For any intervention the first question is how upstream itself would build it — a service with a decorator through dependency injection, a workbench contribution, a registry, an extension point, a `product.json` field, a built-in extension; the answer is the shape of own code. The second question is which seam of the catalogue connects it. A patch is the answer only where no seam exists.
facts.MI-PATCH-IS-A-GRAFT: A patch carries an import or a single call that delegates into own code — at most three lines of code between the markers, comment lines aside — and never logic. The patch creates the seam; own code fills it. Codkit's `verify` enforces the budget on patches of type `hook`.
facts.MI-OWN-MIRRORS-UPSTREAM-TAXONOMY: Own code keeps upstream's folder taxonomy (`common`, `browser`, `node`, `electron-main`; `services/*`, `contrib/*`), one composition root per process, upstream's naming (`*.contribution.ts`, `*Service.ts`), upstream's disposables and event discipline, and upstream's lint and layering rules with the single authorship-header exemption.
facts.MI-SERVICE-OVERRIDE-REACH: Replacing a service through a late `registerSingleton` reaches the renderer and the extension host only: the main process, the shared process, the server and the CLI assemble their services explicitly and never read the registry, and the product service is set explicitly everywhere. In those processes the channel is a graft into the service-assembly function, not a registry call.
facts.MI-UPSTREAM-HAS-A-PARALLEL-SYSTEM: The upstream tree's own second product — a top-level directory above the workbench with its own entry files, `services/`, `contrib/`, a layers document and import-pattern targets of its own — is the precedent a product's own layer follows and cites in reviews.
facts.MI-NO-SLOP: Literal minimality that produces one unreadable file is a violation, not a virtue. A pattern — bridge, adapter, decorator, state, command, registry — is welcome exactly where it matches an upstream idiom, and out of place where it does not.

features.title: 10. A feature is one folder behind a flag

facts.MI-FEATURE-IS-A-FOLDER-WITH-A-FLAG: A new feature of the product is one own folder (`contrib/<feature>/` or `services/<name>/`) and one flag declaration. Where the toggle can be live — everything the feature adds is registered as a disposable — it is live; a feature is created when its flag turns on and disposed when it turns off.
facts.MI-FLAG-LAYERS: Flag sources form layers with a fixed precedence: a build value (from `product.json`, immutable at runtime) → a system policy → a remote-forced value → the user's setting → a remote default → the declaration's default. A build value cannot be undone by any other layer: that is what makes a security feature a property of the build.
facts.MI-COLD-FEATURES-ASK-FOR-A-RESTART: A feature that cannot toggle live — a service override registered at startup, a graft, main-process behaviour — is declared cold: it freezes its value at startup and, when the live value differs, asks for a restart the way upstream does.
facts.MI-REMOTE-IS-A-SOURCE: A server that switches flags centrally is one more source behind the same port as the user's setting; its snapshot applies as one transaction, and the same port drives an internal switching interface before any server exists.

facts.MI-GRAFT-SET-CONTENTS: The constant graft set of a fork consists of: the import-pattern block for the own directory, shaped like upstream's own top-level layer (several targets with their allowed imports, one per sub-layer); the authorship-header exemption; the indentation exclusions for extensions upstream's hygiene does not know (`.toml`, `.csv`, `.license`); one resource glob per bundling pipeline for own assets; and an XLF resource branch only when the product exports XLF. Its size does not grow with the volume of own code.
facts.MI-HEADER-EXEMPTION-FORM: The authorship-header exemption is one data line in upstream's copyright filter; the formatting of own files is covered by the separate lint run, which reads its own filter.

facts.NEVER-DESCEND-A-LAYER-WITHOUT-A-NAMED-RE: Never descend a layer without a reason in `reason` named in the terms of the decision tree.
facts.NEVER-OMIT-A-REQUIRED-FEATURE-FOR-MINIMA: Never omit a feature the product requires in the name of minimality — choose the least invasive form of it instead.
facts.NEVER-COUNT-OWN-AS-FREE: Never count own code as free: coupling is measured by what it leans on upstream, not by its directory.
facts.NEVER-THROW-FROM-OWN-AT-MODULE-EVALUATIO: Never throw from own code while a module is evaluated.
facts.NEVER-CHANGE-AN-NLS-KEY-WITHOUT-A-PACK-D: Never change an nls key in a patch without a recorded language-pack decision.
facts.NEVER-CARRY-THE-SEAM-MAP-ACROSS-A-PIN-UN: Never carry the seam map onto a new pin unchecked.
facts.NEVER-RESTATE-THE-LAYER-LADDER: Never restate the codkit layer ladder in a product's specs — cite `LAYER-CHOICE-RULE`.
facts.NEVER-PUT-LOGIC-IN-A-GRAFT: Never put logic into a patch: a graft imports or calls own code and nothing more (§9).
facts.NEVER-COUNT-A-BUILD-FLAG-AS-OVERRIDABLE: Never let a lower layer undo a build value of a flag (§10).
facts.NEVER-DETECT-UPSTREAM-API-AT-RUNTIME: Never probe the shape of an upstream API at runtime to survive its change: put the dependency behind an adapter and let the compiler and the contract tests fail loudly (§9).
